assumptions.claim: KeyWidth must be a multiple of 64 (EccDataWidth) to avoid integer truncation in ECC word calculation.
assumptions.risk: EccWords will truncate if KeyWidth is not a multiple of 64, causing ECC data misalignment across shares and CDIs, potentially undetected data corruption.

assumptions.claim: LfsrWidth must be even to produce integer EntropyWidth.
assumptions.risk: An odd LfsrWidth causes fractional EntropyWidth, leading to truncated EntropyRounds and potentially broken PRNG reseed scheduling.

uncertain_points.claim: KeyWidth may not be a multiple of 64, causing ECC word misalignment across Shares and CDIs.
uncertain_points.cond: When KeyWidth is configured to a non-multiple of 64.
uncertain_points.risk: ECC check bits could be applied to wrong data chunks, causing silent data corruption in key material.

formal_sketch.consequent: KeyWidth may not be a multiple of 64, causing ECC word misalignment across Shares and CDIs

uncertain_points.risk: If en_i is not properly used to gate all sensitive state transitions, operations could execute in unauthorized lifecycle states, exposing keys.

security_implications: Secret key material (root_key_i, kmac_data_i) is present in the interface. The output wipe_key_o is intended to zeroize keys; if not driven correctly, key material could persist. Error inputs (shadowed_update_err_i, etc.) and fault outputs aggregate integrity errors; if error handling logic is flawed, undetected faults could lead to bypass of security checks. The lifecycle enable en_i controls global operation; misuse could allow key operations in unauthorized lifecycle states.
